body:
Merged, thank you! This is exactly the missing half of ff-tracking.

I measured both tracks the same way, and the numbers explain your "DO NOT UNMUTE" pretty well:

| | LUFS | true peak | <120 Hz | 120 Hz–2 kHz | 2–5 kHz | >5 kHz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| my sfx.py | -14.0 | -0.8 dBTP | -5.3 | -3.5 | **-6.7** | -13.7 |
| your Slab score | -10.7 | -1.0 dBTP | -1.9 | -5.7 | **-13.8** | -14.7 |

(dB of total energy per band.) Mine put about 7 dB more into the harsh 2–5 kHz range, plus a steady 50 Hz hum and a 7.8 kHz whine. Yours is heavier and much softer there. And the camera driving the mix (pan from the tracked box, filter from the zoom, tears on the lock frames) is a lovely idea.

I added a credit and a short license note to the README (slabkit is GPL-3.0 and not vendored; your script, project and WAV are under the repo's MIT, as you offered). Shout if you want it worded differently.

Want to make #3 of the series together from the start? Your score in Slab, my picture in fframes, both reading one timeline. I'll hop on the Discord.
thanks for writing this up, it's linked from the README as the how-it-was-made for the score. closing so it reads as docs, not an open task 🙏
Merged, thanks Marcin! A full Rust score with exact Python parity is amazing work 🦀

Thanks @kvnloo, this is clean work: the backend switch reads well and the CPU lens path keeping the SkSL shader is a nice touch. Built and tested on macOS, Metal path unchanged. Mark it ready when you're done and I'll merge it.
